statement: Add combines the target's shape with the operator's shape through an associative link, leaving both as separate editable elements.
superiority: Boolean via exact kernel with robust error report and persistent link.

acceptance.sketch: Add two overlapping cubes: resulting volume = union volume within 1e-9.

notes: CORRECTED — read Solid Operation Types; the page describes Addition as adding the target's shape to the operator's; the link stays live and the operator is not modified or deleted.

statement: Subtraction cuts the operator's shape out of the target element while the operator remains unchanged and may be hidden by layer or shown as wireframe.
superiority: Subtraction is non-destructive and shows operator ghost.

acceptance.sketch: Subtract sphere from box: volume = V_box - V_sphere within 1e-9.

notes: CORRECTED — read Solid Operation Types and About Solid Element Operations; hiding or wireframing the operator is done through its layer, not a per-operation option.

statement: Subtract the operator extended infinitely upwards from target (e.g. clearing space above a shaft).
superiority: Direction can be any vector, not only upward.

acceptance.sketch: Extruded subtraction removes everything above operator footprint.

notes: VERIFIED — read Solid Operation Types; 'subtraction with upward extrusion' also removes the operator's vertical projection up to the top of the target.

statement: Subtract operator extended infinitely downwards from target.

acceptance.sketch: Downward extruded subtraction cuts below.

notes: VERIFIED — read Solid Operation Types; 'subtraction with downward extrusion' removes the projection down to the bottom of the target.

statement: Keep only the volume common to target and operators.

acceptance.sketch: Intersection of cubes offset by half yields half-cube volume.

notes: VERIFIED — read Solid Operation Types; Intersection keeps only the part common to target and operator.

statement: Add operator volume extended upwards to target.

source.ref: Solid Element Operations: Add with Upwards Extrusion

acceptance.sketch: Added column continues to the top.

notes: REJECTED: Solid Operation Types lists exactly five operations (subtraction, subtraction with upward or downward extrusion, intersection, addition); there is no addition with extrusion.

statement: Add operator volume extended downwards to target.

source.ref: Solid Element Operations: Add with Downwards Extrusion

acceptance.sketch: Downward add extends the target below the operator.

notes: REJECTED: Solid Operation Types lists exactly five operations; no addition with downward extrusion exists in Archicad 30 help.

statement: Store selected elements as targets and others as operators in a floating palette, where a role may hold several elements, stored sets can be re-selected, and an operation type is executed in one click.

acceptance.sketch: 2 targets with 1 operator: each gets cut.

notes: VERIFIED — read Solid Element Operations Palette (Get Target/Operator Elements, Select Stored Targets/Operators, Execute) and Solid Operation Example; roles may be chosen from different windows or stories.

statement: Support nested solid operations where an element is both target and operator, taking care that the result depends on the order in which the operations are applied.

acceptance.sketch: Reordering switches result consistent with math.

notes: CORRECTED — read About Solid Element Operations; nested operations are supported and order matters, but no explicit operator-ordering control is documented.

statement: Allow solid operations on eligible construction elements chosen in any model window, while Morphs use separate non-associative Boolean commands.
superiority: Universal eligibility with clear refusal reasons.

acceptance.sketch: Wall minus morph succeeds; zone as target refused with reason.

notes: CORRECTED — read About Solid Element Operations and Boolean Operations with Morphs; walls, roofs, slabs, stairs, beams appear in examples but no full eligibility list is given; Morph Booleans are permanent, not linked.

statement: Let operators be hidden by layer or drawn as wireframe in 3D after the operation without undoing the cut, while plan display of target and operator is unaffected.

acceptance.sketch: Hidden operator invisible in 3D.

notes: CORRECTED — read About Solid Element Operations, Solid Operation Types and Layer status; wireframe/hidden is a layer property; hidden operators vanish from the Floor Plan and cannot be edited until the layer is shown.

statement: Report failing operations and their reasons, and highlight conflicting elements.

source.ref: Solid Element Operations: Status Information and Error Reporting

acceptance.sketch: An invalid operator raises an error naming the element.

notes: REJECTED: no help page documents failure reporting or conflict highlighting for Solid Element Operations; the only related note is that a beam operator with lower 3D priority than its target appears to have no effect.

statement: Trim selected elements to a roof or shell acting as trimming element, choosing which side of the trim remains in manual mode, or let selected roofs and shells trim each other and the other selected elements in automatic mode.

source.ref: Trim Elements to Roof: Manual Trim

acceptance.sketch: Trimming a wall to a 30 degree roof makes the top slope exact.

notes: CORRECTED — read Trim Elements to Roof or Shell, Manual Trim and Automatic Trim; trimming body options (pivot lines down, contours down, downward or upward extrusion, editable) set direction; trims are associative.

statement: Clear a single or all connections of selected elements (trim, merge, solid operation, curtain wall join) from a connection grip list or a Clear All Connections command.

acceptance.sketch: After removal the wall top returns to its story height.

notes: CORRECTED — read Managing Element Connections; no command literally named Remove Trim exists; the X icon per connection or group and Connect > Clear All Connections sever trims, merges and solid operations.

statement: Let slabs act as targets or operators in solid operations, for example subtracting a stair with upward extrusion from a slab, while only roofs and shells may be trimming elements.

acceptance.sketch: A wall passing through a slab opening is trimmed at the slab top.

notes: CORRECTED — read Solid Operation Example, Trim Elements to Roof or Shell and Stair Endings and Connections; stairs join slabs/walls via solid operations; a 'Trim to Slab' command does not exist.

statement: Link the top of a wall, column, zone or stair to a story above, optionally with an offset, so that its height follows later story changes.

source.ref: Define Toplink for construction elements and zones

superiority: Top link is a visible constraint.

acceptance.sketch: Wall top follows slab elevation change.

notes: CORRECTED — read Define Toplink for construction elements and zones; connecting walls to roofs is done with Trim to Roof/Shell, and to slabs with Adjust Elements to Slabs; this row now captures the top link.

statement: Let layer intersection groups decide which colliding elements may connect, and use junction order to settle equal-priority beams or walls.

acceptance.sketch: Column and wall: higher priority passes through.

notes: CORRECTED — read Use layers to prevent intersections and Specific Element Intersections and Junctions; group 0 elements never intersect; different group numbers prevent connection; no 'Connection Priority' item found.

statement: Resolve junctions of colliding walls, beams, columns, slabs, roofs, shells and morphs by building-material intersection priority, cutting lower-priority skins with higher ones in all model views.

acceptance.sketch: Material priority 10 over 5: junction cut as expected.

notes: VERIFIED — read Basic Intersection Principles and Intersection Priority (Building Material); priorities run 0-999; identical priorities follow Morph > Column > Beam > Slab > Wall > Shell > Roof.

statement: Keep solid operations in model-based views (3D, generated sections and details) while the floor plan view of target and operator stays unchanged, with section windows needing a rebuild to show the result.

acceptance.sketch: The cut shows the fill of the target material.

notes: CORRECTED — read Solid Operation Types; no cut-plane fill choice is described for SEO; the page states the Floor Plan view of both elements is unaffected and sections must be rebuilt.

statement: Apply priority-based intersections uniformly to basic, composite and complex-profile elements, using the building material of each skin.
superiority: Same interplay for any structure type.

acceptance.sketch: Composite wall SEO keeps skins.

notes: CORRECTED — read Basic Intersection Principles; the structure type affects junctions (skin-level cleanup) but is not described as an SEO option.

statement: Keep the shape produced by a solid operation permanently by saving the 3D elements as a library object, since the operation result is otherwise only a live link.

acceptance.sketch: The resulting Morph volume equals the SEO result volume.

notes: CORRECTED — read About Solid Element Operations; the page names Save 3D Elements as Objects (GDL object) to keep the result; converting the SEO result straight to a Morph was not found.

statement: Use terrain mesh as target in SEO to create excavation.

source.ref: Solid Element Operations: Mesh as Target

acceptance.sketch: Excavation volume equals the computed cut volume.

notes: REJECTED: the help does not list a mesh as a solid operation target; Intersecting Elements That Don't Clean Up states that Mesh is not supported in intersections.

statement: Operate with many operators quickly; recalculation should be incremental.

source.ref: Solid Element Operations: Performance with many operators

acceptance.sketch: 200 operators complete in time budget.

notes: REJECTED: no help page describes performance, incremental recalculation or operator-count limits for Solid Element Operations.

statement: Give roofs and shells a trimming body whose direction can be pivot lines down, contours down, downward extrusion, upward extrusion or (for shells) an editable shape, shown optionally in 3D.
superiority: Visualise trimming bodies always and allow free-form bodies for roofs too, with live feedback on what will be cut.

acceptance.sketch: Roof with downward-extrusion body trims a wall that crosses it: wall portion above the roof plane is removed, below stays, for any pitch.

notes: ADDED+VERIFIED — read Define Trimming Bodies; default roof body is pivot lines down, shell body is downward extrusion; set in Roof/Shell Settings Model panel; shown via On-Screen View Options.

statement: Merge colliding roofs, shells and morphs with other elements so that priority-based junctions apply, or merge trimming bodies of several roofs and shells before trimming other elements.
superiority: Detect required merges automatically and flag colliding elements that would not clean up.

acceptance.sketch: Morph and composite slab merged: skin intersections follow material priority; unmerged they do not clean up.

notes: ADDED+VERIFIED — read Merge Elements: Roofs, Shells, Morphs and Merge Trimming Elements; at least one element must be a roof, shell or morph; connection shows in the connections list.

statement: Report element quantities as net (reduced by solid operations, openings and trims) and gross (ignoring them) so schedules can use either.
superiority: Compute both values from one exact solid model and show the delta caused by each operation.

acceptance.sketch: Wall volume with a subtract operator of volume 0.2: net volume = gross - 0.2; gross unchanged.

notes: ADDED+VERIFIED — read Solid Operation Types (Interactive Schedules paragraph) and Column Listing Parameters; net listings account for Solid Element Operations, gross ones ignore them.

statement: Offer Boolean union, subtract and intersect on Morphs that give a permanent single Morph result rather than a live link.
superiority: Offer a switch between permanent and live boolean results on the same command.

acceptance.sketch: Union of two cubes of side 1 overlapping by 0.5 gives one morph of volume 1.5; subtract removes the operator morph from the model.

notes: ADDED+VERIFIED — read Boolean Operations with Morphs; result attributes follow the last selected Morph; subtract deletes the operator; non-solid morphs are warned about.

statement: Join a stair to adjoining slabs and walls through solid operations, since a stair has no automatic associativity with other 3D element types.
superiority: Make stair-to-slab openings an automatic, parametric connection that follows stair edits.

acceptance.sketch: Stair rising through a slab with subtraction with upward extrusion: slab hole matches the stair outline projected up to the slab top.

notes: ADDED+VERIFIED — read Stair Endings and Connections and Solid Operation Example; stair settings define flight/landing endings, while connection to slab or wall uses Solid Element Operations.
